h.select_rule: Discard any hypothesis whose condition is the edited field's own current value, or whose condition merely disables or disconnects the edited component. From the rest, keep 10 with distinct mechanisms and field pairs, favouring those where an informed expert could plausibly bet on either direction.
h.strategy: Two patterns are banned because experts find them obvious: (1) conditioning on the current value of the same field being edited, which just restates that upgrading a weak setting helps more than upgrading a strong one; (2) conditions that make the edited component unused, unreachable or inert. Instead, each hypothesis must link two DIFFERENT fields that interact through a non-trivial mechanism, such as substitution between parallel routes, a capacity already supplied elsewhere, one part acting as a bottleneck for another, or interference that turns a usually helpful edit harmful. No condition setting may appear in more than two hypotheses. Use the gaps and negated assumptions as the source of each idea. In each 'why', name the mechanism and explain why the opposite direction is also a priori plausible.

hyps.why: A conv on edge 2 creates a deep conv-conv serial path whose optimization benefits most from an input-to-output identity shortcut.
With node 2 cut from the output, edge 3 is one of only two routes to node 3, so adding conv capacity there matters more.
A downstream conv can turn pooled node-2 features into a useful multi-scale signal instead of passing blur to the output.
Pool-then-conv along 0->1->3 acts as a larger-receptive-field path, softening the usual cost of pooling on edge 0.
A conv already on a parallel in-edge to node 3 supplies output capacity, giving diminishing returns to a second conv.
Parallel in-edges to node 2 substitute for each other, so a conv on edge 2 helps less when edge 1 is already a conv.
When edge 2 already feeds node 2 with a strong conv, removing edge 1 costs little and reduces dilution of the summed features.
When node 2 carries a blurred pooled signal, removing its route to the output costs less and may remove interference.
A second identity route into the output is largely redundant and lets shallow features dominate the node-3 sum.
A skip on edge 2 forwards upstream edge-0 conv features into node 2 and onward, reusing capacity already supplied.
